title: The Homogenizing Effect of Large Language Models on Human Expression and Thought

bias_targets.methodology: Synthesizing studies that analyze LLM-generated and polished texts (such as Reddit posts, news articles, and personal essays) to measure the reduction in lexical diversity, semantic variance, and the erasure of sociolinguistic markers tied to author characteristics like age, gender, personality, and political affiliation.

Reviewing evaluations that use instruments like the World Values Survey and the Moral Foundations Questionnaire-2 (MFQ-2) across high-temperature model runs to demonstrate that LLM outputs disproportionately align with WEIRD (Western, Educated, Industrialized, Rich, and Democratic) perspectives and marginalize alternative cultural worldviews.

Examining literature that compares LLM problem-solving and reasoning patterns against human cognitive tasks to highlight a convergence on uniform, dominant reasoning templates (such as chain-of-thought) and a lack of natural, culturally varied problem-solving heuristics.

Analyzing studies that use identity prompting to evaluate whether LLMs capture the heterogeneity of specific demographic groups (e.g., individuals with visual impairments) or reduce them to fixed, essentialized out-group stereotypes.
